meta.title: Ondra Co-Create Flow
meta.description: A co-creation flow for Ondra (L9 extension pool): who proposes, who edits, and when to stop, when two people make something together. Four beats in a fixed order — brief, draft, review, settle. The proposer only sets the goal and the acceptance criterion; the maker only produces and revises. Roles are rotated by the state machine and cannot be assigned by the caller, so 'the same person both proposes and revises' is structurally impossible. The edition count has a hard cap, and once it is reached only settling is allowed: the cap counts editions rather than speaking turns, because turns can be inflated by anyone — one question and one answer already flip a round — while an edition only increments when a version is actually handed over. A revision must build on the previous edition, since starting a fresh draft breaks the edition numbering and nobody can tell what is being revised. handoff() must carry an edition number and rejects a mismatch outright, so when two callers edit at once the later one fails loudly instead of quietly overwriting the other. Settling does exactly one thing: it forces the caller to ask, in so many words, 'is this version final?', and then stop. This plugin has no finalized state at all — final is the literal false in the type — because finalizing is a human answer, and a flow that can answer on someone's behalf will start doing so two rounds in. The goal and the handoff note are validated but never retained; only their character counts are kept. The text itself belongs to the caller and the memory system, with its own visibility rules and right to be forgotten. It generates no content (that is the dialogue chain), installs no timers, never sends messages on its own, renders no UI, and writes nothing to disk.
